Re: Public Records Act Request

Dear Alpine Community Planning Group Members,

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I am writing to request a copy of the records detailed below.

I am researching how the Alpine Community Planning Group (ACPG) conducts its business on the part of the residents of Alpine in preparation for publication of an expose. To that end, I request the following records:

1. All Alpine Community Planning Group Agendas and Minutes from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025.

2. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another member(s) of the Alpine Community Planning Group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

3. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another government agency, including between the group members and the County of San Diego from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

4. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and any member of the public, including between the group members and individuals/entities with business before the group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

Please note that the Public Records Act allows a member of the public to request records by describing their content, rather than asking for specific documents by name; an agency that receives such a request must “search for records based on criteria set forth in the search request.”

Public records represent “any handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photographing, photocopying, transmitting by electronic mail or facsimile, and every other means of recording upon any tangible thing any form of communication or representation, including letters, words, pictures, sounds, or symbols, or combinations thereof, and any record thereby created, regardless of the manner in which the record has been stored.” (Government Code section 7920.545.)

1. This request applies to all records in your agency’s possession, including documents created by a member of another government agency or a member of the public.

2. If specific portions of any documents are exempt from disclosure, please provide the non-exempt portions.

3. Please provide entire documents, even if only parts of them are responsive to this request.

If you maintain records or data in electronic format, please provide them in that same format.

1 California First Amendment Coalition v. Superior Court, 67 Cal.App.4th 159, 165-66 (1998).
2 See California State University v. Superior Court, 90 Cal. App. 4th 810, 824-25 (1999).
3 Gov’t. Code § 6253(a). versions are acceptable) to avoid copying costs.
4 If you are unable to reproduce electronic records in electronic form, please provide a reason for doing so.

I request that you waive copying fees because I have limited resources, and the information requested will be used in the public interest to further the public’s understanding of the local community planning group action. None of the information obtained will be sold or distributed for profit. If you are unable to waive the copying fees, and you anticipate that these costs will exceed $50, or that the time needed to copy the records will delay their release, please contact me so that we can arrange to inspect the document or decide which documents we wish to have copied. Otherwise, please copy and send them as soon as possible. Please respond to this request within ten (10) days, either by providing all the requested records or by providing a written response setting forth the legal authority for withholding or redacting any document and stating when the documents will be made available.

If you require any clarification in identifying responsive documents or focusing this request, please contact [redacted]. Please send all records responsive to this request to Louis Russo.

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

[redacted]

emails.body:
From:                                                       Leroy, Chiara
Sent:                                                         Friday, October 25, 2024 8:57 AM
To:                                                            Barbara Orozco-Valdivia
Subject:                                                   List of Equity Impact Grant Winners - Cohort #1

Good morning Barbara,

It was so nice spending time with you on Wednesday, catching up and talking shop. As promised, here
is the list of Equity Impact Grant winners for cohort #1. The cohort #2 winners should be announced
next week or so.
Building Justice (HoMEwork) – A Southeast San Diego organization that supports people
transitioning out of incarceration by prioritizing their personal development, creating a support
system, and providing opportunities to amplify their voices and inﬂuence policy decisions.
First Gen Scholars – An organization helping ﬁrst-generation, low-income Black, Latinx, and
Southeast Asian students navigate the college admissions process and graduate debt-free.
Free Thought Revolution – A community-driven eﬀort to “bridge the divide of humanity
through storytelling, community, and social action.” In addition to their podcast, their vision
includes educational initiatives and housing programs to provide a safe space for marginalized
individuals to engage in healing and community-building.
Garden 31 – This organization trains and mentors youth and adults that are considered at-risk,
formerly incarcerated, justice-impacted, and socioeconomically disadvantaged in regenerative
agriculture, sustainable food systems, and life skills to improve community health and wellness.
Inner-Tribal Treatment – To address the needs of the Native American population impacted by
the opioid crisis, this organization provides one of the only culturally-based treatment
programs in Southern California.
Lived Experiences – A North County community-based organization that utilizes data-proven
methods to advocate for change by investing in people’s microsystems and addressing the root
causes of physical and emotional trauma.
Majdal Arab Community Center of San Diego – Through advocacy and cultural programs, this
East County organization works to empower and uplift the Arab community in San Diego.
Paddle for Peace – An organization conceived to create a nurturing space where BIPOC children
could not only access coastal environments for recreation, physical ﬁtness and mental healing
but also envision and explore careers in Marine Biology and Environmentalism. To date, they
have provided over 600 ﬁrst time coastal experiences for BIPOC, underserved youth.
San Diego Community Birth Center – This is the only Black-owned birth center in San Diego
County, providing access to midwifery care, doula and lactation services, among other
resources that ensure healthy births.
San Diego Black LGBTQ Coalition – A volunteer-led organization that not only serves over 500
Black LGBTQ people and families yearly but works to address the acute needs of the Black
transgender community.

Sharing some additional resources that may be of use:
Community Leadership Teams, including links to each region’s website (which has each region’s
priority areas listed), and the 2008-2025 Community Health Assessments
Equity Impact Report, provides “baseline synopsis of the impact of systemic racial inequities
throughout our County”

Please let me know if there’s anything else that I can share with you.
Talk soon and good luck canvassing!

Warmly,

Chiara

emails.subject: Report on SANDAG's September Meetings to the Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
emails.body:
Good Afternoon APG Members,

September 13th and 27th reports are in two segments below:

*September 27th Meeting (Eileen):*

Due to a communication error I was not given complete instructions to
attend the Sept. SANDAG board meeting remotely and be promoted to a
separate screen.

It was difficult to hear the conversations and I was unable to
participate. I am attaching the agenda for your review.

On a different subject… As Robin has let you know, Congressman Issa held a
meeting with the mayors of most of the cities, along with SANDAG’s new CEO,
to discuss their transportation and other needs.  Unfortunately the APGs
which represents ALL of the County’s unincorporated residents was not
included.

When Robin notified the Congressman’s staff, we were given the impression
that this would be rectified and another meeting would be scheduled with us.

Instead, we have been invited to a mixer/open house for their new offices
in Santee “for invited guest” with no plans to sit down for a discussion.

This is a concern on many levels.

Attached please find the emails that Robin and I have both sent.  (Included
at end of this email.)

We’ll let you know if/when we have any updates.

*September 13th Meeting (Robin):*

*SANDAG's CEO, Mario Orso:*
Mario Orso confirmed he had received the request from the APG to attend a
joint meeting between Congressman Darrell Issa, APG members and himself.
Hannah Stern of SANDAG will coordinate with the APG and Congressman Issa to
ensure attendance at a future meeting.

Background: The Congressional Representative (Darrell Issa), who's district
encompasses the vast majority of the unincorporated area, held a meeting
during his open house in Escondido. In a private meeting before the event
Congressman Issa had invited SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso and staff to discuss
transportation and funding. The Congressman had included Mayors from his
district. There was no County representation nor unincorporated area
through the APG.
This oversight was immediately brought to the attention of the Congressman
and his office staff by the APG. The APG sent a letter to the Congressman
and copied Mario Orso. See complete letter at end of this email.

*SR 125 Investigation Summary:*
"The investigation found ETAN's Fastlane financial reporting cannot be
relied upon, and the Finance department lacks adequate internal controls,
including proper review and supervision, to ensure SR 125 financial
information is accurately recorded and reported. The report recommends an
independent assessment of the Finance department's policies, procedures,
and practices."

*Office of the Independent Auditor - FY 2024 Annual Investigations Report:*
The Independent Performance Auditor, Courtney Ruby, made a defining
statement of the state of SANDAG's contracts invoicing and payment process;
- The system is broken. -
"Most concerning is the finding that invoices totaling $13055,123 or 32.39%
of the sample size, did not include sufficient documentation to determine
what work was completed by contractors."
This report included 7 recommendations by the auditor.

APG Comment to Board: Thank you for the great report. I have done accounts
payable in the past. With a more than 32% failure to follow the process for
accounts payable, I am going to assume there is some overpayment of
taxpayer dollars. And then, recommendations 1 through 7 - I did not see a
plan for recovery or potential recovery of taxpayer dollars. Is there
overpayment out there and how we would know if documentation was not done
correctly? Is there a plan for this? Thank you. (2:10:30)

SANDAG response (Courtney Ruby): When we evaluated the invoice payments.
This would be with the project managers and contracting whether the
information was there. Then it was passed on for payment. So we're seeing
insufficient documentation and it's being passed on for payment. We would
have to drill down further in relation to determine was the work done or
not done. This procedure did not go to evaluating whether everything going
back to project managers that would have been a different audit. A
different audit, this was looking to see based on their procedures. Are
they following their procedures? Is the documentation there? So, in order
to quantify that, that would take, that would be a different audit.

*Public Comment:*
Paul The Bold, comment to the Board: Does SANDAG really work for the whole
county? You've got Robin Joy Maxson sitting over there. Theoretically,

*SANDAG Board Actions and Discussions - March 2024*

*SANDAG Retreat 2024:*
March 8th meeting - a Board Retreat held at the Salt Drift Pointe, 536 13th
Street, Imperial Beach from 8:30 to 3:30. Both the APG Representative
(Robin Maxson) and Alternate (Eileen Delaney) attended and participated in
the team building activities. The goal of the Retreat was to build a
regional planning mindset for the Board members and to develop a set of
criteria/traits for the next SANDAG CEO. Recruiting and interviewing has
narrowed the candidate field to six individuals.

*Caltrans:*
Roy Abboud and Mario Orso - communicated to the APG Rep that Caltrans had
2.6 billion in funding for the unincorporated area projects. Also, that
they would be "speeding up" projects on the SR 67.

*125 Toll Road Action Plan:*
March 22nd Meeting - Coleen Clementson reported that SANDAG had signed the
contract with the group (unnamed) that would be running the new back-office
system and that it would be up and running by the end of the year.
Independent Performance Auditor - Courtney Ruby will be presenting the
results of the audit at the next Board meeting. (As it turned out a Special
SANDAG Board meeting was called for March 29th to specifically discuss the
results of this internal audit.)
Report on options discussed with South Bay leaders for early pay off of 125
Toll Road would be brought forth in a future meeting.

March 29 Special Board Meeting - The report from the Office of the
Independent Performance Auditor released a report on March 25th resulted in
a Special meeting of the Board to be called.  This report was previously
sent to APG members in a separate email, but here is the link:
https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/about/office-of-the-independent-performance-auditor/reports-and-documents/sr-125-investigation-report-final.pdf

The report revealed ongoing, egregious lack of oversight and a pattern of
failure to take action to correct a multitude of issues with operation of
the 125 Toll Road.
Board members questioned every aspect contributing to this situation:
Why wasn't the Board informed of the back-office discrepancies in tolls
collected and toll user accounts?
Why have we signed a contract with the same company that did not deliver on
the contractual requirements?
Why would we contract again with companies that did not collect nor record
tolls correctly?
What is the criteria for selecting a company for the contract?
Why wasn't it reported to the Board that tolls stopped being collected due
to equipment disconnect sooner?
Why is SANDAG using QuickBooks for accounting purposes?
Who in SANDAG's executive leadership knew of these issues and when?
What is SANDAG's Whistle Blower policy?
Why did SANDAG allow a culture of intimidation to exist with respect to the
former CEO?
Why were financial reports repeatedly corrected and the issues leading to
faulty numbers not corrected instead?
How much money has the contractor been paid for the 125 Toll Road and for
other projects they manage, for example the I-15 managed lanes.
How can we ensure that the same accounting issues have not occurred with
the I-15?
How much money in tolls was lost overall?

Board member comments were:
"After I pick up my jaw from the floor I have a few questions."
"This isn't just a black eye for SANDAG, but two black eyes."
"We need to investigate potential fraud."
"We need to rebuild trust in SANDAG."

The Independent Performance Auditor's recommendations were accepted by the
Board and more Board actions and answers to questions and concerns would be
forthcoming at the April 12th regular Board meeting.

*Report of SANDAG's Draft Fiscal Year 2025 Budget Program - Capital
Projects:*
SANDAG reported on the DRAFT FY 2025 Budget. The presentation included the
project and funding allocation of both TransNet and non-TransNet funded
projects. The hand out (see attachment) was a visual overview of the
projects and location - Note the lack of projects planned (funded) in the
unincorporated area of the County. Based on this discrepancy in funding for
the unincorporated area and for areas of North County the Board heard many
complaints from its own members.

APG comment to Board: "Good morning. Thank you. Representing the
unincorporated area where we're 500 thousand strong. I understand that we
use the limited funds where it can do the most good. But I would like to
remind everyone to keep in mind that we do have a large population outside
of the populated corridor. And, that in addition to the 500 thousand, we do
have thousands of visitors on the weekends. So, I see a lot of funding for
bikeways which is good for health and greenhouse gas reduction. But I see
very limited funding for our Vision Zero Plan to reduce highway severe
injuries and fatalities. I don't see a lot of money in the unincorporated
area where all of the visitors are coming on the weekends and where there
is a tremendous amount of pressure on those roadways. Also, I don't see
that a priority is being given to wildfire evacuation. And, with two
unsuccessful wildfire evacuations in '03 and '07 it is not a matter of if;
but when we will have another one. Right now it is green, but it won't be
that situation in June. I would like to know how SANDAG determines the
funding allocation - how do they decide that balance between a population

prioritization process. The annual budget looks at when those projects are
meant to be open; like if a project is meant to be open in 2035 we need to
get started on that

emails.subject: Loveland Parallel Trail. Other options/ Fish Stocking.
emails.body:
Carlos Quintero,Sweetwater Authority General Manager. 

Hello GM Quintero.

How are you? 
As you know ,what actual lake users wanted and want at Loveland was more access. Both you and Andrew Hayes frequently said there are no limits on the possiblities with the funding. I fail to see how the parallel trail makes any sense. For the path shown The elevattion drop is the same as the existing trail.It requires new brush and tree clearing whereas as switch back stays even in the "user defined " area. It requires maintance the same as the exsting trail, and a trash can, or two.It costs more with the 250K bridge plus 200k "parallel trail" plus maintenance than the $400k bridge.As much as I hate to say it the $400k brige makes more sense. Not ast much sense as a switch back and pipe hard scape but more than the current proposal.
Please consider more practical and cost effective option or go with the big bridge and use the additional 50k to put a pedestrian gate on the east end of the lake.
Alternately,  please find a cost effective crossing at the ravine, I have more ideas,  and stock threadfin shad heavily when weather and other conditions are good for it. .DFW will allow that and these forage fish  are good for birds and other wildlife as well as fish. 
Even with the SDGE easement approved, access from the south side is needed. 
Please call me if you want to talk about any of this or email.

A pedestrian gate here and any forward momentum along the shoreling  at this yellow line  is well within the easement and it's legal to walk on Japatul Road.

Thank you,
Russell Walsh.
